q: Which of the following spaces is an entrance structure?
n: A porch is a roofed entrance structure attached to a house, sheltering the front door. Terraces, lanais and patios are outdoor living spaces. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: What is the minimum comfortable distance between the closet and the edge of a bed?
n: About 3 ft (900 mm) between the bed and a closet front lets a person pass and open doors or drawers comfortably. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Bedroom Clearances).

q: What is the standard height of a vanity table?
n: Per the exam key, a vanity table is about 75–88 cm high. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Bathroom and Dressing); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: Which architectural feature refers to a series of aligned doorways in adjacent rooms, creating a continuous visual axis through the entire suite?
n: An enfilade is a suite of rooms whose doorways line up on one axis, giving a continuous view through all of them. It is typical of Baroque palaces. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: What is the minimum dimension of a toilet and bath?
n: Based on the minimum T&B dimension from NBCP which is 900m or roughly 36 inches. Sec. 806 requires a toilet and bath to have a least dimension of 0.90 m, about 36 in, and a minimum area of 1.20 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 806.

q: If 50% of the governor’s office is to be installed with carpet tile flooring, what is the approximate number of standard carpet tiles needed to cover it?
n: The governor's office is 40.5 m x 12 m = 486 sqm, and half of it is 243 sqm. 243 sqm / 0.25 sqm per 50 x 50 cm tile = 972 tiles. Source: Carpet and Rug Institute, CRI 104 (Commercial Carpet Installation); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 5 – 2-STOREY PROVINCIAL CAPITOL BUILDING

Design Problem. The Provincial Government of Occidental Mindoro, headquartered in the capital town of Mamburao, has long operated from an aging capitol complex that no longer meets the spatial, functional, and safety demands of a growing and diversifying population. Built decades ago, the current capitol structure suffers from outdated facilities, limited space for administrative expansion, and insufficient resilience against climate-related hazards such as typhoons, earthquakes, and flooding—risks that frequently affect this side of Mindoro Island. In response, the provincial government has initiated plans to construct a new 2-storey provincial capitol building within a newly designated government complex in Mamburao. The new structure is envisioned as a symbol of progress, institutional integrity, and service-oriented governance. It will house key executive and legislative offices, administrative departments, and public service counters, while also accommodating disaster-resilient infrastructure, efficient workflows, and sustainable design strategies reflective of the province’s agricultural and environmental character. The provincial government has commissioned an architect to lead the project from conceptual design to coordination with structural engineers, planners, and contractors. The goal is to deliver a modern, functional, and civic-minded government center that can serve the present needs of Occidental Mindoro’s citizens while anticipating future demands in governance, development planning, and community engagement. Following a series of planning sessions and consultations, the following spatial requirements for the 2400sqm building were identified:
1. The ground floor is accessed through 15m x 15m main lobby connected to the 15m x 375sqm atrium. To the left side of the atrium and lobby is the executive offices which has an area of 22.5m x 40m and to the left are the following:
1. circulation and support spaces - 135sqm
2. administrative offices - 427.5sqm
3. session hall - 337.5 sqm
2. On the second floor are the following spaces
1. governor’s office - 40.5m x 12m with an overlooking view of the people’s plaza
2. administrative offices - 19.5m x 34m on the right side of the governor’s office
3. circulation and support spaces - 135sqm on the northeastern side
4. hallway - 3m wide all around the atrium and connecting to the bridge going to the multilevel parking building
Site Features. The parcel allocated for the new provincial capitol building of Occidental Mindoro is along the Capitol Road and near the entrance of the provincial capitol complex. Oriented towards the north-west direction, the capitol road is the main thoroughfare of the capitol complex which measures 1.3 hectares. The capitol building is to be placed on the north-east side of the road facing the new people’s plaza on the other side. The building has a 60m frontage same with the plaza in its front. Its facade faces the SW direction. The area is relatively flat. The parcel for the capitol building has an allocated 50m x 3300sqm area, a corner lot bounded by a 12m road on its front and a 10m on its left side. A multilevel parking building is to be built on the opposite side of the 10m wide service road with a bridge that connects to the 2nd floor of the main capitol building. The parking building has a TGFA of 1,360sqm.
Design Objectives. The primary objective is to create a modern, resilient, and dignified 2-storey provincial capitol building that reflects the institutional identity and service-oriented mission of the Provincial Government of Occidental Mindoro. The design must support efficient administrative workflows, ensure accessibility and public engagement, and incorporate disaster-resilient features suited to the province’s climate risks. Special emphasis will be placed on organizing executive, legislative, and public service spaces around a central atrium, fostering openness and transparency. The building shall also establish a strong civic presence along Capitol Road, with strategic integration to the adjacent People’s Plaza and direct connection to the multilevel parking facility via a second-floor bridge, ensuring seamless circulation within the new capitol complex.

q: Given a 0.32% reinforcement ratio, what is the weight of reinforcement needed for the framing beam of the atrium opening on the 2nd floor? The beam section is 250mm x 400mm.
n: Framing beam length is equal to the perimeter of the atrium opening. Based on the layout, the perimeter is 80m. The reinforcement ratio is basically the percentage of beam section dedicated for reinforcement. If the beam section area is 0.1sqm (0.25 x 0.4), the area of the reinforcement is 0.1sqm x 0.32 = 0.032sqm. The total volume of the reinforcement is 0.032sqm x 80m = 2.56 cu.m. Therefore, the total weight of reinforcement needed is 2.56 cu.m x 7850 kg = 20,096kg. The beam section is 0.25 m x 0.40 m = 0.10 sqm, and 0.32% of it is steel. Per the exam key, 20,096 kg over the 80 m atrium perimeter. Code note: the exam's solution multiplies by 0.32 instead of 0.0032. At a true 0.32% ratio the steel is only about 20 kg. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 409 (Reinforcement Ratio); steel unit weight 7,850 kg/cu.m.

n: If you get the correct layout and add the atrium space, you should be able to get the same area. The total area of 898.5sqm. q: Minimum seats for typical gang chairs.
n: Gang (beam) seating usually starts at three seats per beam. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Public Seating); BIFMA X5.4 (Lounge and Public Seating).

q: For industrial occupancies, the computation of the maximum occupant load shall be:
n: Industrial occupancies are computed at 9.3 sqm per person for maximum occupant load. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Occupant Load Factors – Industrial); NFPA 101, Table 7.3.1.2.

q: Pipe color coding for pipes carrying acidic substances.
n: Per the exam key, pipes carrying acids are color-coded yellow, the color for dangerous or corrosive contents. Source: ASME A13.1 (Scheme for the Identification of Piping Systems); PNS/ISO 14726.

q: Which of the following is ideal when considering the smoke developed index of a building material?
o: Equal to the flame spread index
n: A lower smoke developed index is ideal, as it means the material produces less smoke during combustion, improving visibility and reducing health risks during fire emergencies. A lower smoke-developed index is better, since less smoke means better visibility for escape and less toxic exposure. Interior finishes are limited to indices of 450 or less. Source: ASTM E84 (Surface Burning Characteristics); RA 9514 (Fire Code) RIRR (Interior Finish).

q: What is the required no-build zone distance from a fault trace based on Philippine building regulations?
n: PHIVOLCS recommends a no-build buffer of at least 5 m on both sides of an active fault trace. Source: PHIVOLCS, Guidelines on Active Fault Buffer Zones; Valley Fault System Atlas.

q: Minimum written notice period before contract termination.
n: Per the exam key, contract termination requires written notice of at least 15 days. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 202 / Architect's Guidelines (2016) (Termination of Contract); Civil Code of the Philippines (obligations and contracts).

q: Mountable curbs are only allowed for sidewalks with width of
n: Per the exam key, mountable curbs are allowed only where sidewalks are 5 m wide or more. Source: PD 957 / BP 220 Revised IRR (Curbs and Sidewalks); DPWH Design Guidelines.

q: Since the front setback was waived in the commercial area, what is the maximum projection over the sidewalks?
n: On a 12 m RROW, a projection over the sidewalk may be at most 1.30 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 811 and Table VIII.6 (Projections over Public Sidewalks).
scenario:
DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 4 – 3-STOREY FOOD COMMERCIAL BUILDING

Design Problem. A well-established food organization, KusinaKomunidad, known for supporting local culinary startups and foodpreneurs, has acquired a prime lot along Maginhawa Street in Quezon City—an area celebrated for its diverse and creative food scene. To further its advocacy and provide space for emerging food businesses, the organization plans to develop a 3-storey commercial building dedicated to food-related enterprises. The building will house 12 rentable commercial units, with 4 food spaces per floor. These spaces are intended for small to medium-sized food ventures such as cafés, take- out counters, dessert shops, and themed dining stalls. The building design must allow for flexible interior layouts, adequate ventilation systems, and shared access to essential food service facilities. The organization also aims to incorporate design elements that reflect the community-driven and innovative spirit of Maginhawa. KusinaKomunidad has commissioned an architect to handle the project from conceptualization and design development to coordination with contractors. The goal is to create a functional, visually appealing, and accessible food hub that supports both new and growing food businesses in Quezon City. Following several planning sessions, the following requirements were identified:
1. The ground floor shall be composed of an open parking area on the right side of the lot measuring 17m x 238sqm. Adjacent to the parking lot is three-floor building structure having a footprint of 33m x 396sqm and with a firewall on the left side. The ground floor spaces of the building is composed of a staircase on both ends, 4 units of 7m x 84sqm rentable space for food establishments. The stairs on both ends measure 2.5m x 4.5m connected with a long pathway to the RROW sidewalk. 2m setback shall be provided at the back.
2. On the 2nd floor of the building is an outdoor dining area which can also hold mini concerts and bands. The area has an ample 28m x 5m dimension spanning across the four rentable food spaces. These spaces have an area of 49sqm each and have direct access to the front alfresco dining area.
3. On the 3rd floor is an even smaller footprint with 4 units of rentable commercial spaces. Each of them measures 7m x 5m deep connected by a 2m walkway accessible through the two stairs on both ends. These walkways shall be covered and has an overlooking view to the Maginhawa street and the dining area below.
Site Features. The project will be built in an elongated lot with a 50m wide frontage. Located in a special commercial zone in Quezon City, the building height limit is 3 floors. The lot is relatively flat and is serviced by the 12m-wide Maginhawa Street. Adjacent establishments are all commercial spaces except for the rear side which is bounded by a private residential lot. 2m rear setback is to be provided and front setback was waived due to the commercial nature of the area.
Design Objectives. The objective is to create a cohesive, community-oriented commercial building that fosters collaboration, innovation, and growth among small food enterprises. The design should promote flexibility in tenant fit-outs, support efficient circulation, and provide engaging public spaces that encourage social interaction and local cultural expression. Special attention shall be given to optimizing the elongated lot, integrating sustainable and low-maintenance materials, and ensuring compliance with commercial zoning while maintaining a vibrant, approachable street presence.

q: What is the minimum width of national roads as per DPWH?
n: Per the exam key, national roads are given a minimum right-of-way of 20 m. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines, Criteria and Standards (Road Classification and ROW); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII.

q: What is the maximum projecting signs allowed over the Maginhawa street?
n: Per the exam key, a projecting sign over this street may extend at most 1.20 m. Source: PD 1096 (NBCP), Ch. 20 (Signs) and 2004 Revised IRR, Rule XX.

q: Which of the following is not ISA?
n: The impervious surface area (ISA) covers paved, unroofed surfaces such as driveways, unroofed porches and paved gardens. A grassed patio is pervious, so it is not ISA. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Table VIII.1 (ISA).

q: In geodetic engineering, what are established reference positions on the ground used for surveying and mapping called?
n: Control points and benchmarks are different because control points provide known horizontal and/or vertical coordinates for general surveying and mapping, while benchmarks are specifically used for elevation reference only. Benchmarks are a type of control point, but not all control points are benchmarks. Control points are established, precisely surveyed ground positions (horizontal and vertical) used as references for surveying and mapping. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying; DENR-LMB Manual for Land Surveying.

q: Which type of survey is primarily conducted to determine and establish property boundaries for land ownership and titling?
n: A cadastral survey defines property lines and legal boundaries, serving as the basis for land titling, registration, and resolving land ownership disputes. Cadastral surveys determine and establish property boundaries for ownership, titling and tax purposes. Source: DENR-LMB Manual for Land Surveying in the Philippines (Cadastral Surveys).

s: Design Problem 2 – BerDeliver Trucking and Manufacturing Hub
q: What approximate number of parking slots provided on the center island if 45- degree diagonal parking layout is to be used?
n: Per the exam key, a 45° angled bay on the central island holds about 32–36 cars. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking slot dimensions); Neufert, Architects' Data (Car Parks).
scenario:
DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 2 – BERDELIVER TRUCKING AND MANUFACTURING HUB

Design Problem. A local entrepreneur, known for his innovation in green transport, successfully built an eco-friendly delivery vehicle that gained attention for its low emissions and practical design. With growing interest in sustainable logistics, he saw an opportunity to expand his vision by entering the trucking industry, aiming to provide cleaner and more efficient freight services across Luzon. He established a new business called “BerDeliver Trucking Industry", with a mission to lead the transition toward eco-conscious logistics in the country. Alongside this, he developed a mobile app called “BerDeliver - Your Sustainable Delivery App”, designed to connect clients to a fleet of low-emission trucks for real-time freight booking and tracking. The company’s main freight hub will rise in the Sta. Rosa Industrial Hub in Laguna, a strategic location that will also house his existing green motorcycle manufacturing facility. With this integrated approach, BerDeliver aims to become a key player in sustainable transport solutions in the Philippines. The following are the predetermined requirements of the project:
1. The front zone (Zone 1) is a 2,560sqm parking lot inclusive of the 10m wide service road. The layout is a one-way double-loaded parking scheme with a central angled parking bay. Entry to the parking lot is through the service road, looping around the length of the parking area, then exiting again to the service road.
2. The middle zone (Zone 2) is the manufacturing facility area, a large 7,040sqm area with a building footprint of 4,680sqm. The 2-storey manufacturing facility includes spaces for storage, chassis assembly line, battery assembly line, installation section, final assembly line, testing and quality control zone and dispatch area.
3. The rear zone (Zone 3) measures 80m x 80m and shall be the allocated for the headquarters of the BerDeliver trucking service. 50% of the zone is the building footprint - a 3-storey office building with storage facilities. The remaining shall be for the parking space and various auxiliary spaces including the service road. The service road services all the three zones and the future expansion to the rear of the lot.
Site Features. The proposed site is a rectangular regular lot with an area of 1.6 hectares sloping downwards at 7% towards the rear side of the lot. The 80m frontage of the lot is facing a 15m-wide national highway. The left and right sides of the lot are bounded by other privately owned lands. The adjacent lot to the rear side is reserved for future expansion of the BerDeliver. Located in a medium-intensity industrial zone in Sta. Rosa City, the project is considered to store and handle flammable materials or liquids.
Design Objectives. q: Which parking layout is typically used in tight residential settings where two vehicles park one behind the other in a shared space?
n: Tandem parking is a practical solution for space-constrained areas, allowing two vehicles to share a single elongated space by parking one behind the other—commonly used in townhomes, condominiums, and private driveways. Tandem parking puts two cars one behind the other in a single long slot. It is common in tight residential layouts. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Parking); NBCP Rule VII (parking provisions).

s: Design Problem 2 – BerDeliver Trucking and Manufacturing Hub
q: What is the frontage of the manufacturing facility?
n: Per the exam key, the 7,040 sqm middle zone measures 80 m x 88 m, so the answer is 88 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII (Lot Dimensions).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 2 – BERDELIVER TRUCKING AND MANUFACTURING HUB

Design Problem. A local entrepreneur, known for his innovation in green transport, successfully built an eco-friendly delivery vehicle that gained attention for its low emissions and practical design. With growing interest in sustainable logistics, he saw an opportunity to expand his vision by entering the trucking industry, aiming to provide cleaner and more efficient freight services across Luzon. He established a new business called “BerDeliver Trucking Industry", with a mission to lead the transition toward eco-conscious logistics in the country. Alongside this, he developed a mobile app called “BerDeliver - Your Sustainable Delivery App”, designed to connect clients to a fleet of low-emission trucks for real-time freight booking and tracking. The company’s main freight hub will rise in the Sta. Rosa Industrial Hub in Laguna, a strategic location that will also house his existing green motorcycle manufacturing facility. With this integrated approach, BerDeliver aims to become a key player in sustainable transport solutions in the Philippines. The following are the predetermined requirements of the project:
1. The front zone (Zone 1) is a 2,560sqm parking lot inclusive of the 10m wide service road. The layout is a one-way double-loaded parking scheme with a central angled parking bay. Entry to the parking lot is through the service road, looping around the length of the parking area, then exiting again to the service road.
2. The middle zone (Zone 2) is the manufacturing facility area, a large 7,040sqm area with a building footprint of 4,680sqm. The 2-storey manufacturing facility includes spaces for storage, chassis assembly line, battery assembly line, installation section, final assembly line, testing and quality control zone and dispatch area.
3. The rear zone (Zone 3) measures 80m x 80m and shall be the allocated for the headquarters of the BerDeliver trucking service. 50% of the zone is the building footprint - a 3-storey office building with storage facilities. The remaining shall be for the parking space and various auxiliary spaces including the service road. The service road services all the three zones and the future expansion to the rear of the lot.
Site Features. The proposed site is a rectangular regular lot with an area of 1.6 hectares sloping downwards at 7% towards the rear side of the lot. The 80m frontage of the lot is facing a 15m-wide national highway. The left and right sides of the lot are bounded by other privately owned lands. The adjacent lot to the rear side is reserved for future expansion of the BerDeliver. Located in a medium-intensity industrial zone in Sta. Rosa City, the project is considered to store and handle flammable materials or liquids.

The client commissioned a full-service architectural firm to design a freight hub that efficiently integrates trucking operations with an existing green motorcycle manufacturing facility. The design challenge is to ensure smooth logistics flow, functional zoning, and sustainability, while maintaining clear separation between industrial activities and support facilities within the site.

q: Where does an architect secure a Height Clearance Permit (HCP)?
n: HCP means Height Clearance Permit and ATO means Air Transportation Office (which is now the CAAP or Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines) A Height Clearance Permit is secured from the civil aviation authority. The Air Transportation Office (ATO) has been the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) since 2008. Source: RA 9497 (Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008); CAAP height clearance regulations.

q: When connecting a new drainage pipe to an existing manhole, what measurement is needed to ensure proper flow alignment?
n: Invert elevation is the reference point for aligning drainage pipes at the correct depth to maintain continuous flow toward the outfall or treatment system. The invert elevation (the inside bottom of a pipe) is matched at the manhole to set the slope and flow alignment of the new drain. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Storm Drainage); DPWH Design Guidelines (Drainage).

q: Which of the following is not a typical component of a French drain system?
n: A French drain consists of a gravel-filled trench, geotextile fabric, and a perforated pipe to redirect water. Asolid concrete base is not used, as it would block water infiltration and drainage. A French drain is a trench of gravel wrapped in geotextile around a perforated pipe. A solid concrete base is not part of it. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Subsurface Drainage).

q: Which of the following trees is endemic to the Philippines?
n: Mangkono (Philippine ironwood) is an endemic tree species found only in the Philippines, known for its extremely hard wood and limited natural range, making it both ecologically significant and conservation-sensitive. Mangkono (Xanthostemon verdugonianus), the Philippine ironwood, is endemic to the Philippines. Narra is native but also grows elsewhere in Southeast Asia. Mahogany and acacia are introduced. Source: DENR, Philippine Native Trees; DENR DAO 2017-11 (Threatened Species).

q: Which of the following best distinguishes an endemic tree species from a native tree species?
o: Both are found only in rainforests
Endemic species are found only in one specific geographic location
Endemic species are more useful for timber
n: Endemic species are unique to a particular region and are not naturally found anywhere else, while native species occur naturally in a region but may also exist in other parts of the world. An endemic species occurs naturally only in one geographic area. A native species occurs naturally in an area but may also be found elsewhere. Source: IUCN Red List terminology; DENR Biodiversity Management Bureau.

q: According to the new BP 344 provisions, what is the required clear level space before and beyond a door?
n: The amended BP 344 IRR requires a clear level space of at least 1,800 mm × 1,800 mm before and beyond a door. Source: BP 344 2024 Amended IRR, Doors and Entrances, item 2.6.

q: According to the new BP 344 provisions, what is the minimum clear width required for all doors?
n: The amended BP 344 IRR requires all doors to have a minimum clear width of 900 mm (1,800 mm for double-leaf doors). Source: BP 344 2024 Amended IRR, Doors and Entrances, items 2.1 and 2.3.

q: According to the new BP 344 provisions, at what height should door handles, pulls, and latches be centered?
n: Under the amended BP 344 IRR, door handles, pulls, latches and lever locksets are centered 900 mm above the finished floor. Source: BP 344 2024 Amended IRR, Doors and Entrances, item 2.11.

q: According to the new BP 344 provisions, what is the required minimum dimension for turnabout spaces in corridors?
n: The amended BP 344 IRR requires corridor turnabout spaces of at least 1,800 mm × 1,800 mm, spaced at most 12,000 mm apart. Source: BP 344 2024 Amended IRR, Corridors, item 5.2.

q: According to the new BP 344 provisions, what is the maximum allowable angle of inclination for an escalator?
n: The amended BP 344 IRR limits escalators to an inclination of 30°. Source: BP 344 2024 Amended IRR, item 10.3.

q: What is approximate number of gypsum boards for the ceiling of the secondary room at the 2nd floor?
n: The area of secondary room is 4m x 4m so 16sqm. The standard area of commercial gypsum board is 1.2m x 2.4m (2.88sqm). Therefore, the number of gypsum board is 16sqm / 2.88sqm = 5.55sqgm or 6 pcs. 16 sqm / 2.88 sqm per board = 5.6, so 6 boards. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Ceiling Boards).

Design Problem. Mr. Shikahn is an Indian businessman who met Maria Santos, a 30-year old marketing manager from Dasmariñas, Cavite, at a Manila tech conference. They eventually got together and decided to marry in Maria’s hometown. Shikahn purchased a 0.0351ha interior lot adjacent a road facing commercial strip lot. He intends on making the Philippines their permanent home. Together they commissioned a three-storey house with 360-view on the 3rd floor. They were the one of the few first homeowners in the semi-exclusive residential area in General Trias, Cavite. Maria and Mr. Shikahn both love the outdoors so they wanted a home that connects them to nature. To achieve this, they listed the following requirements that their architect took note:
1. The ground floor building footprint maximizes open spaces. Instead of maximizing the allowable building footprint, 1.00m was added to the minimum required setbacks all around the building creating a wide looped open yard for the couple to enjoy.
1. Ground floor features a spacious living room at the front left, seamlessly flowing into a central dining area. The kitchen, located at the back right, connects to a cozy patio through sliding doors. A staircase and utility area occupy the right front, with a common toilet centrally positioned nearby.
2. The back patio features a cozy, covered space with outdoor seating, potted plants, and direct kitchen access through sliding doors, perfect for relaxed dining and social gatherings.
2. The second floor features a well-planned layout with two bedrooms and a family room. The master bedroom, situated at the back right, measures 5m x 4m and includes a private toilet and bath (2m x 2.5m), offering comfort and privacy. The secondary bedroom, located at the front left, is 4m x 4m, spacious enough for a queen-sized bed. Centrally positioned, the family room measures 4m x 5m, serving as a cozy gathering space. A common toilet and bath (2m x 2m) is conveniently placed in the hallway, accessible from both the family room and the secondary bedroom.
3. The third floor features a versatile entertainment room, a guest bedroom, and a spacious covered balcony. The entertainment room, located at the front, measures 5m x 6m, providing ample space for leisure and social activities. Adjacent to it, the guest room (4m x 4m) offers comfort and privacy for visitors. At the back, the covered balcony spans 4m x 6m, perfect for outdoor lounging, with seating and a partial garden setup. The balcony is accessible through sliding doors from the entertainment room, seamlessly blending indoor and outdoor spaces while offering panoramic views and a relaxing ambiance.
Site Features. A 7m wide, 8m long private road services the interior lot, also serving as its frontage. The private road connects to a 10.5m wide RROW oriented SW to NE. The lot is located on the NW side of the RROW, measuring 18.0m x 351sqm. The lot is separated from the RROW by an 8m deep 25m long commercial strip placed on both sides of the private road. Drainage naturally flows towards the north side at 2%.
Design Objectives. The three-storey residence shall blend Filipino and Indian cultural influences, reflecting the couple's shared identity and love for the outdoors. The design will feature open, airy spaces connecting indoor and outdoor living, with cultural elements like capiz windows and intricate patterns. Distinct family spaces will ensure privacy while common areas foster togetherness, creating a harmonious and welcoming home.

q: If one-storey 37.5sqm footprint extension is to be added on the left side, what is the allowable maximum length of the abutment?
n: Remember that the zone is R-2, so the maximum allowable firewall length is 80% of the side length which is 15.6m (19.5m x 0.8). Take note that while the question mentioned the 37.5sqm extension which provides a 12.5m firewall, it is NOT the allowable maximum length of the abutment. In R-2, an abutment may run at most 80% of the side property line: 19.5 m x 0.8 = 15.6 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 708 (Firewalls) and Table VII.4.

q: If footing tie beam will be provided around the building footprint, what the approximate volume of the concrete in cu.m. needed for the footing tie beam if the section is 250mm x 300mm?
n: lt was mentioned that the footing tie beam is around the building so we have to know the perimeter length of the building footprint. The footprint measures 12.50m x 12.0m so the perimeter is 49m. We now approximate the volume by multiplying the beam section to the length of the beam. Approximate concrete volume = 0.25m x 0.30m x 49m = 3.675 cu.m. The footprint perimeter is 2 x (12.5 m + 12 m) = 49 m. 0.25 m x 0.30 m x 49 m = 3.675 cu.m. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Concrete Beams).

q: What should be the maximum height of the sidewalk opposite the curb side if the sidewalk width is 1.20m?
n: Remember that as per NBCP, the maximum slope of a sidewalk towards the curb shall be 1:50 or 2%. Therefore, the highest point shall be 1.20m x 0.02 = 0.024m above the curb. With a maximum cross slope of 2% for accessible sidewalks, a 1.20 m sidewalk rises 0.02 × 120 cm = 2.4 cm from curb side to the opposite edge. Source: BP 344 IRR (walkway cross slope 1:50); DPWH Design Guidelines (Sidewalks).

q: What should be considered when using terracota tiles as an interior accent wall?
n: Terracotta is porous. Indoors it absorbs stains and moisture, so it needs sealing and the right placement. Source: Natural Stone Institute and TCNA Handbook (Terracotta Tile Care); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What is the standard maximum floor area coverage of an ordinary-hazard fire sprinkler?
n: NFPA 13 allows a standard spray sprinkler to protect up to 130 sq ft (about 12 sqm) in ordinary hazard occupancies. Source: NFPA 13, Table 10.2.4.2.1(b) (Protection Areas – Ordinary Hazard).

q: Standard distance of a wall switch from the latch side?
n: Wall switches are mounted on the latch side of the door, about 150–200 mm from the jamb, where the hand finds them on entering. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Housing (Electrical Layout); Philippine Electrical Code practice.

q: What is the main benefit of COB type tracklight to other types of tracklight?
n: COB (chip-on-board) LEDs pack many diodes into one dense emitter. That gives a single, concentrated, uniform beam with less multi-shadowing, which is ideal for accent track lights. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (LED Sources); lighting manufacturers' technical notes.

q: Boring tests are required for what types of projects?
o: If building is 3 storeys and above
n: Refer to the National Building Code for this. Per the exam key, soil boring tests are required for buildings of three storeys and above. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule III (Building Permit – Soil Boring Test); NSCP 2015, Sec. 302.

q: How do typical roof ventilators operate to expel warm air from enclosed spaces?
n: Roof ventilators work through natural convection, where warm air rises and escapes through vents without mechanical assistance, promoting continuous air circulation and reducing heat buildup in attic or roof spaces. Turbine roof ventilators are wind-driven and assisted by natural convection. Warm, buoyant air rises and is drawn out without electrical power. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting (Stack and Wind-Driven Ventilation); manufacturers' technical data.

q: FF&E means what in interior design?
n: FF&E means Furniture, Fixtures and Equipment: the movable items specified and procured for an interior project. Source: CSI MasterFormat Division 12 (Furnishings); interior design practice standards.

q: What is the primary use of tectum panels?
n: Tectum panels are primarily used for acoustic control. Made from wood fibers bonded with cementitious material, they absorb sound effectively and are commonly installed on ceilings and walls in gyms, auditoriums, and other noise-sensitive spaces. Tectum (wood-fiber) panels are mainly used for acoustic control. Their porous surface absorbs sound in gyms, auditoriums and offices. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics (Porous Absorbers); manufacturers' technical data.

q: Tectum panels are primarily made from which of the following materials?
n: Tectum panels are made from excelsior, which is wood wool or shredded wood fibers, bonded with a cementitious binder. This combination provides excellent acoustic absorption and durability for ceilings and wall treatments. Tectum panels are made of excelsior (aspen wood wool) bonded with an inorganic cement binder. Source: Manufacturers' technical data (wood-fiber acoustical panels); ASTM C423.

n: Polished concrete, though durable, is vulnerable to damage from acids and harsh chemicals. Without proper sealing, it can stain or deteriorate in industrial settings involving chemical processes.
